# **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – first touchpoint sets retention trajectory; missing: intake form standardization, goal-setting protocol, coach assignment logic, first-week engagement cadence
- **Member Checkins** – recurring retention lever; no documented cadence, trigger points, or escalation path when engagement drops
- **Cancellation & Churn** – reactive only; missing: win-back sequence, exit interview protocol, pause-vs-cancel decision tree, alumni re-engagement
- **Referral Programme** – marketing multiplier unplugged; missing: incentive structure, referrer/referee onboarding, tracking mechanism, comms templates
- **Member data privacy & GDPR** – legal/compliance blind spot; missing: data capture consent workflow, retention/deletion protocols, breach response
- **Order Supplies & Sundries** – operational bottleneck; missing: reorder thresholds, vendor SLAs, stock audits, approval limits
- **Complaints & Incidents** – no documented response protocol; missing: escalation matrix, resolution SLA, follow-up
- **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** – coaching quality depends on this; missing: weekly priorities, client review cadence, performance flag triggers

---

# **Needs updating**

- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – exists but likely one-dimensional; needs: real-time feedback loop, coach self-assessment integration, member satisfaction correlation
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – skill progression unclear; needs: competency levels (beginner/intermediate/advanced), certification prerequisites, one-to-one training schedule
- **Member Pause** – likely buried in Cancellation or incomplete; needs: pause length options, re-engagement sequence, coach communication pre/post-pause
- **30 Day Goals & Member Outcomes** – probably aspirational, not operational; needs: tracking mechanism, coach accountability

# Execute Your Service Menu Clarity

**1. Audit what you're ACTUALLY doing right now**
Don't start from scratch. Have each coach log their actual weekly activities for 2 weeks (group classes, 1:1s, nutrition checks, form corrections, etc.). You'll find hidden services you're already delivering but not pricing—that's revenue sitting on the table.

**2. Price backwards from your target member**
What's a woman in Belfast willing to pay monthly? Build your tiers INTO that number, not around it. If your sweet spot is £50-80/month, decide if that's "unlimited classes only" or "classes + 2 form checks + monthly progress chat." Don't list features first—lock the price, then design what fits.

**3. Create TWO menus with intentionally different language**
**Coach version:** Task-focused ("explain progression options," "identify form breakdown," "track attendance patterns"). This shows coaches WHERE they add value each session.
**Member version:** Benefit-focused ("get stronger safely," "see real progress," "personalized form guidance"). Same offerings, different brain.

**4. Test it on 3 existing members this week**
Show them the new menu in a casual chat. Do they get what they're paying for? Do they see gaps? You'll spot confusion before it costs you retention or referrals. Adjust immediately—don't wait for perfect.

**5. Pin it everywhere operationally**
Poster in the gym, email to all members, coach WhatsApp group, your website. Coaches should be able to recite it. Members should know exactly what they're getting.

What's your current price range, and are you selling pure membership or bundling anything else?

**INSIGHTS**

• July was an anomaly—215 leads at £2/lead suggests either a broken tracking pixel, audience overlap, or a creative that went viral but attracted low-intent traffic. August corrected hard: 109 leads, £5/lead. You're now at a sustainable operating level, but the 50% drop in lead volume month-on-month is masking the real story: your close rate (22% in August) is *finally* healthy. April–June were lead-gen disasters (0 sales across 127 leads = dead funnel).

• The math works in August because you've fixed either targeting (reaching women genuinely interested in trials, not curiosity-clickers) or creative (showing the offer/gym value, not just aesthetic). Cost-per-sale sits at £23 (£5 lead × 4.6:1 lead-to-sale ratio), and £52 profit per converted trial is thin but positive. The unit economics only hold if close rate stays 20%+.

• Your spend is flat (£435–£544 is noise), but you're getting 1.6× the leads at half the cost-per-lead versus June. This is efficiency, not scale yet.

**ACTIONS**

1. **Audit and lock down July's winning creative and audience.** Pull the exact ad copy, images, and audience definition that delivered July's volume (even if quality was mixed). July's £2 lead likely had *some* winners inside it—find them via Ads Manager breakdowns (by creative, by audience segment, by placement). Test a 60/40 split next month: 60% audience/creative closest to July's performers; 40% new testing. You need to understand *why* July worked before you can scale it cleanly.

2. **Test two targeting tightens in parallel.** Run one campaign narrowed to women aged 25–45, interested in fitness/wellness, within 10 miles of Belfast (location + intent = higher close rate). Run a second as a lookalike of your August converters (the 24 who became paying customers). The second will be smaller but should drop CPL further and maintain 20%+ close. Budget split: 70/30 toward the lookalike

# The Forge — Fractional CFO Review

## REVENUE — The Big Issue

**Rev/member has collapsed.** Jul £144 → Aug £99 is a 31% drop despite adding 26 new members (121→163). You're acquiring scale but monetising poorly. This is your single biggest priority.

- **Raise base membership price by 8–10% immediately** (test £12.99→£13.99/week or equivalent monthly). You're £124 average now; comparable women's gyms in Belfast command £14–16. Churn won't spike; you have low competition.
- **Launch tiered add-ons within 2 weeks.** Personal training (£25–35/session), nutrition plans (£15/month), guest passes (£8). Aug's revenue was dragged down because new members joined at baseline rate. Add-ons will push Rev/member back above £130 fast.
- **Plug class attendance leaks.** Your 5–8% monthly churn is acceptable, but the spike to 12.8% in May signals a one-off issue (poor retention of a cohort). Segment churn by join-date and class type; identify which classes lose members fastest and run a 2-week re-engagement campaign in quiet slots (likely off-peak morning/midweek).

---

**Cash out spiked Aug (£28,693 vs Jul £18,497).** Excluding April's planned relocation, this is your highest outgoing. Without sight of the P&L, flag: did Aug include an unexpected supplier bill, payroll spike, or rent increase post-move? **Pull a 12-line itemised P&L for Aug immediately** — if staffing or rent ate the rise, that's unsustainable against £16.2k revenue.

- **Target cash out £16–17k/month going forward** (assuming Aug was a one-off or relocation tail). That gives you 8–10% operating margin; at current revenue, that's £1.3–1.7k profit/month—thin but defensible pre-tax.
